name: NoMachine (NX)
description: A remote desktop tool built on the proprietary NX protocol, tuned specifically for staying responsive over slow/high-latency connections. Free forever for personal use between NoMachine installations; paid perpetual licenses for enterprise/multi-user scenarios.

Wayland Unattended Access.comment: Supported via screen capture, but a known bug can lose the session after restart/logout on GNOME+NVIDIA setups

Frame Rate (FPS).comment: No fixed published figure; the NX protocol prioritizes low latency over a fixed high FPS target

Adaptive Bitrate.comment: Differential encoding and bandwidth-aware compression are core to the NX protocol's design

Multi-User Sessions.comment: Multi-user access is specifically an Enterprise-tier feature, not available in the free personal version

Open Source.comment: The original NX/libNX libraries were GPL open source years ago; current NoMachine releases are proprietary/closed

Microphone Passthrough.comment: Clean host-to-client audio streaming is confirmed; client-mic-to-host passthrough is not clearly documented

Pre-Login Access.comment: Can connect to and unlock the target's actual login/physical desktop session

No Account Required.comment: Direct IP connections work without an account; a NoMachine account is used for cloud-based discovery/relay features

Linux X11: Host.comment: The NX protocol's original and most mature platform, via native X11 proxying/compression

Linux Wayland: Host.comment: Supported via screen capture, with a documented session-detection issue on some GNOME+NVIDIA configurations

Web Browser: Client.comment: No officially documented browser-based client; native apps only

NVIDIA RTX 4090.comment: GPU-accelerated remote rendering is marketed for Enterprise use cases, but no published comparative benchmark table exists

Free Tier.comment: Unlimited, free forever for personal/non-commercial use between NoMachine installations

Team / Business: Monthly.comment: NoMachine sells perpetual licenses, not a monthly subscription model

Enterprise.comment: One-time license pricing scales with edition/features, not a recurring subscription
